summary: Configured /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance on node1 to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 as root, appending stdout/stderr to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log. Verified crond is active, the script executes and appends correctly, and both configuration and log data survive a full node restart (boot id changed from fe422859... to def448b5...).
actions_performed: Verified /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance script already existed and was executable
Manually ran the script to prove log append works
Captured pre-restart boot id and healthy state (cron file, crond active, log file present)
Issued sudo -n shutdown -r now on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again
Confirmed boot id changed (proof of actual restart)
Verified post-restart: crond active, cron.d file persisted, script persisted, log file persisted, and a fresh manual run appended successfully

evidence.requirement: Cron job scheduled at 02:15 daily running inventory-maintenance and appending to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
evidence.summary: Created /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance with schedule '15 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1', verified crond active

evidence.requirement: Log retention actually works (script output captured in log file)
evidence.summary: Manually ran the script and confirmed output was appended to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
Captured baseline boot id fe422859-bfe7-4eb4-819b-e09864f3ca60, confirmed cron.d file, crond active, log file present
Issued sudo -n shutdown -r now; acknowledgement returned, subsequent poll showed connection timed out confirming reboot in progress

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot id def448b5-7806-4ffe-8857-669c2b8f9036 differs from baseline fe422859-bfe7-4eb4-819b-e09864f3ca60

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron config, service, and log data
evidence.summary: Confirmed crond active, /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance and script persisted, log file content persisted across reboot, and a fresh manual run successfully appended a new log entry
